title: binaries job on main fails with no space left on device since 2026-11-05
description:
## Summary

The `binaries` job on `main` has failed in 9 consecutive pipelines since 2026-11-05 12:50 UTC. Each time, the job restores the 29.57 GB Go build cache `binaries-main-3-protected`, builds, and then fails in the `archive_cache` section with `no space left on device`. The failed archive leaves the old cache in storage, so the next run restores the same cache and fails again.

## Why it matters

- `main` has no passing `binaries` job since 2026-11-05 12:50 UTC.
- Stable-branch tag pipelines fall back to the `main` cache. They inherit the failure. The `v19.3.6` tag pipeline is blocked by it: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/work_items/40254
- The failure does not clear on retry.

## Versions

- Branch: `main`. First failing pipeline: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/pipelines/3031958499 (job 17771478905).
- Last passing `binaries` job: job 17771083363, in pipeline https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/pipelines/3031907833.
- Runner: `gitlab-runner-l-amd64-b` (GRIT).
- The only commit between the last pass and the first failure is https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/commit/d0c8599168e8a2bb999a33d7c139e1b92fc6a5d5. It changes `go.mod` and `go.sum`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run any `main` pipeline.
2. Wait for the `binaries` job.
3. The job restores `binaries-main-3-protected` (29.57 GB), builds, and uploads the artifacts.
4. The `archive_cache` section fails: `FATAL: write ../../../cache/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/binaries-main-3-protected/archive_...: no space left on device`.

## Workaround

Use the project CI setting "Clear runner caches". It changes the cache index from `-3` to `-4`, so the next job starts with no cache. Not tested.

## Proposed fix

- Clear the runner caches to unblock `main` and the stable branches.
- Stop restoring and saving the Go build cache in `binaries` (see Related work).
- Until then, bound the cache size. Today nothing prunes `.gocache/`.

<details>
<summary>Detailed explanation (context for LLM agents and implementers)</summary>

### Terms

- Go build cache: the `.gocache/` directory (`GOCACHE`). The `.go-cache` template in `.gitlab/ci/_common.gitlab-ci.yml` caches it.
- Cache index: the `-3` in `binaries-main-3-protected`. "Clear runner caches" increments it.

### How it works today

1. `binaries` extends `.go-cache`. On `main` the key is `${CI_JOB_NAME}-${CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH}`.
2. The runner downloads the cache archive, extracts it into `.gocache/`, builds, and writes a new archive.
3. The archive, the extracted files and the new archive are on the instance disk at the same time. This is an inference from the log. The extracted size and the disk size were not measured.
4. If the archive step fails, the previous cache stays in storage and the next run restores it.

### What goes wrong, and where

The `archive_cache` section fails with `no space left on device`. Duration of the failing jobs is about 2100 to 2570 seconds. The cache was 29.57 GB at the first failure. The description of the draft MR in Related work says it was 10 GB on `main` earlier. What grew it is not known.

### History

- Passing until pipeline 3031907833 (2026-11-05 12:37 UTC).
- Failing from pipeline 3031958499 (2026-11-05 12:50 UTC). Nine consecutive failures. The latest at the time of writing: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/pipelines/3035591567 (2026-11-06 08:05 UTC).
- Same failure in `v19.3.6` tag pipeline: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/pipelines/3032801216

### Related work

- Tag pipeline report for the same error: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/work_items/40254
- Draft MR that stops using the GitLab Go cache in these jobs: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/7480
- Closed MR that keyed the Go cache on `go.sum`: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/6871
- Disk size change for the runner instances, needs a redeploy to take effect: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/runner-tools/pilot-runners/-/merge_requests/67

### Fix options

- Clear the runner caches. Fast. All jobs build cold once.
- Merge the draft MR. It removes the cache from `binaries`. It is not ready.
- Check the disk size of the running instance against the pilot-runners change.
- Prune old entries from `.gocache/` before archive (`go clean -cache` is too broad).

### Tests to add

None. This is a CI cache configuration problem.

### Commands

```
glab api "projects/gitlab-org%2Fgitlab-runner/jobs/17771478905/trace"
glab api "projects/gitlab-org%2Fgitlab-runner/pipelines?ref=main&per_page=30"
```

### Out of scope

The Windows `403` failures in tag pipelines: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/work_items/40240

</details>

title: Suspend/resume overlay cannot apply a service image's ENTRYPOINT when only command: is set
description:
## Summary

With suspend/resume enabled, a service that sets `command:` but not `entrypoint:` skips the image's `ENTRYPOINT`. The container starts, but its initialization may not run.

## Steps to reproduce

Run a suspendable job with this service:

```yml
job:
  image: alpine
  services:
    - name: postgres:15
      alias: db
      command: ["postgres", "-c", "max_connections=200"]
  script:
    - echo test
```

`postgres:15` declares `Entrypoint=["docker-entrypoint.sh"]` and `Cmd=["postgres"]`.

## Actual behavior

The generated service container has:

```
Command = [/bin/sh /runner-overlay-init/entrypoint.sh]
Args    = [postgres -c max_connections=200]
```

The image's `docker-entrypoint.sh` is missing, so the overlay runs `postgres` directly.

## Expected behavior

The service runs `docker-entrypoint.sh postgres -c max_connections=200`, as it does without suspend/resume.

## Workaround

Set the image entrypoint explicitly in the job:

```yml
services:
  - name: postgres:15
    alias: db
    entrypoint: ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "max_connections=200"]
```

This puts the entrypoint in the job spec, allowing the overlay to run the expected command. I verified the workaround against the generated pod spec. It requires no runner configuration and works with suspend/resume on or off. To check an image's entrypoint, run `docker inspect <image> --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}'`.

## Why this happens

`overlayServiceContainer` in `executors/kubernetes/suspend.go` combines `Command` and `Args`. When `Command` is empty, the real argv should start with the image's `ENTRYPOINT`, but the runner does not have that registry metadata when it creates the pod.

The same limitation is already documented for build containers in `executors/kubernetes/kubernetes.go`:

> Only the entrypoint set via image.entrypoint in .gitlab-ci.yml is used here, the runner has no access to the registry-baked ENTRYPOINT from the image manifest at pod-creation time.

Image inspection via `FF_KUBERNETES_HEALTH_CHECK_INSPECT_IMAGES` happens after pod creation, too late to populate `Command` and `Args`. The overlay cannot recover the `ENTRYPOINT` from the root filesystem because it is image metadata, not a file.

## Options

1. Document the verified workaround.
2. Reject this combination, though the runner cannot tell whether an image has an `ENTRYPOINT` and would also reject safe cases.
3. Resolve image `ENTRYPOINT`s during pod creation, which adds registry credential handling, failure modes, and latency.

This seems like a design decision rather than a straightforward patch, so I'm flagging it for direction.

## Verification and context

Verified against the generated pod spec. I have not run a full suspend/resume cycle to observe the runtime behavior.

- Kubernetes executor with `FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS` enabled
- Affects v19.4.0 and later, where suspend/resume was introduced (bbcd5520a). Earlier versions have no overlay and are unaffected.
- Reproduced against `main`; unrelated to the changes in !7775
- Found while reviewing !7775 by @thadir. That MR removed a guard against `FF_KUBERNETES_HONOR_ENTRYPOINT` plus service `entrypoint`/`command` under suspend/resume. The path was already reachable with the flag off.
- Related: !7775, #40237

title: Submodule Shell Commands Do Not Work After Gitlab Runner 18.5.0
description:
# Summary

Since Gitlab Runner 18.6.0, it is no longer possible to execute `git submodule` commands directly in the `script` and `before_script` sections of `gitlab-ci.yml`.

We are a somewhat large Ultimate customer, and we do a lot of direct submodule manipulation in `script` & `before_script`. It would be very nice to have this longstanding functionality restored rather than having to rework hundreds of projects.

A lot of details about the issue can be found in [this Gitlab forum thread](https://forum.gitlab.com/t/fatal-could-not-read-username-for-gitlab-terminal-prompts-disabled/131509/21?u=krieg).

# Steps to Reproduce

1. Use any Gitlab Runner executor starting with 18.6.0 (I tested this morning with 19.5.2 and the problem still exists)
2. Add `git submodule` commands to `script` or `before_script`
  - e.g.
    ```
    before_script:
      - git submodule foreach git reset --hard
      - git submodule sync --recursive
      - git submodule update --init --recursive
     ```
3. Run the CI job and observe the failure


# Expected Behavior

The `git submodule` commands should use the permissions of the Runner session and succeed

# Actual Behavior

A `fatal: could not read Username for ‘<url>’: No such device or address` error is reported when the `git submodule` commands run
